sourceInformation.source: ice hockey (over the top arcade style)
sourceInformation.plan: PLAN.md (the plan given with this build)
sourceInformation.genre: Sports: three-a-side arcade hockey with goalies, a Cup Run story, exhibition, practice and online sessions
sourceInformation.perspective: TV broadcast camera (threequarter, 2.5D) with an overhead view (V)
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge engine v0.85.2 (handoff package), plain JavaScript; AI Hub client session.js 1.4.0 (verbatim); Node 24 for headless tests; Playwright 1.63.0 with Chromium for the browser and hub checks
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine's PS1-era pixel art and humanoid rigs; hockey gear, rink, nets and crowd drawn in code
sourceInformation.animation: The engine's procedural humanoid rig and poses (skating, cheer, stagger, down, save)
sourceInformation.audio: All synthesized in code: chip sound effects, babble voices in Animalese style, one match song
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub shared-world session, 1 to 4 seats: the host's copy runs the match, the others send their input and show its snapshots
sourceInformation.testing: one command (tests/run.mjs): headless Node checks, a Chromium smoke test, and the AI Hub harness run as 1 to 4 copies with latency and loss
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux (WSL2); Chromium, headless, through Playwright

testingFeedback: 11 issues found in the game build. The online work added no failures: the hub harness passed all four rounds on the first run.
4 were game-breaking: a hang in an angle wrap, goalies going NaN from a duplicated data key (and an unset target), the net box blocking every goal, and a draw crash that only the browser run caught.
Most helpful: headless match runs that counted shots, saves, goals and goal-line crossings. They exposed the net and goalie bugs.
Least helpful: scene checks that only confirm the scene name. Headless runs skip drawing, so they passed while a draw crashed.
engineFeedback: Most liked: the sports kit as a base, the TileMap with runtime cell changes (map.set for broken glass), and game.advance for headless play.

Stuck or guessed wrong: the pixel fonts had no PlayStation symbols; E.store needs localStorage (stubbed in the tests); the Dialog voice option and the mouse-aim call were taken from the docs and not fully verified.
Most important thing built myself: the rink's collision (a wall grid from the rounded rectangle), the puck and goal-line rules, and the skater and goalie AI.
Hardest: finding the right call in a 14,700-line engine file, and that headless runs skip drawing, so draw bugs need a browser.
Engine change: PlayStation symbols added to both pixel fonts (they drew as ?). Logged in ENGINE-CHANGES.md.
One change: run scene drawing in headless mode (or offer a draw-check mode) so screen code can be tested without a browser.
promptFeedback: Liked most: the explicit rules (one test command, no subagents, file names and sections) and the plan's numbers.
Confusing: the title rule (TASK asks for 50 random titles, STAGE says use the plan's title), and a 1,500-line plan for a medium-effort build.
Hardest: fitting the full plan into one build (online play, seven drills, AI tuning without watching the play live).
Would change: name a minimum vertical slice and what can be cut, and say whether online play must work for the game to count as done.

aiHub.name: Ice Breakers
aiHub.tagline: Three a side. Goalies. Glass. KABOOM.
aiHub.description: Three-a-side arcade hockey with goalies, breakable glass, fights and KABOOM. A five-game Cup Run, exhibition, seven drills, and online sessions for 1 to 4 players.
aiHub.controls: Move: left stick or WASD; Pass: cross or J; Shoot: square or K (hold for slapshot); Deke: circle or L; Lob or gloves: triangle or I; Turbo: R2 or Shift
